isa_target.source: docs/implementation-plan.md#1.1 p0 row: RV64IM_Zicsr_Zifencei, M-mode, bare-metal, single hart, two execution clusters, cacheless ordered memory endpoint

derived_notes: p0 deliberately does NOT claim A, C, F, D, V, S, U, Sv39 or any cache; docs/implementation-plan.md#1.1 lists these as forbidden early claims.
Two clusters exist in p0 because the execution fabric (I-022..I-032) is in scope for the p0 gate; clusters are an internal structure and are not architectural state.

The test protocol lives in RAM, not in the test_harness device region: HTIF, and therefore Spike, can only poll a tohost address that is real memory, and placing tohost in memory is the universal bare-metal convention. The test_harness region remains mapped for the harness to recognise, but TOHOST itself is an ordinary memory word the harness observes after the run.
